item.title: Brisk 0.9.3
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • A rule can now cover several folders and subscriptions at once, such as a Tech folder and a news folder. Click the Scope button in the rule editor and check the ones you want; leave everything unchecked for all subscriptions. A rule matches articles from any of the selected places.
  • To start a rule for several sources, ⌘-click them in the sidebar, then right-click and choose "Add Rule for N Selected…".
  • Existing rules keep their scope. Deleting a folder or subscription removes it from a rule's scope; a rule whose scope becomes empty is deleted rather than widened to all subscriptions.
  • Fixed: right-clicking one of several items selected in the sidebar now shows the menu for the whole selection (mark all as read, refresh, move to folder, add rule) instead of just the clicked item.

item.title: Brisk 0.9.2
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Rule words are now entered as chips. Type a word and press Space, comma, or Return to turn it into a chip; select a chip and press Delete to remove it. This fixes typing in the rule word fields, where Space didn't work with Korean input and only a couple of characters could be entered.
  • Every rule can have a name, set when you create it. The name appears in Settings > Rules and, for "Collect in List" rules, in the sidebar. Leave it empty to show the rule's words as before.

item.title: Brisk 0.9.1
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Keyword rules now have three word fields: "All of" (every word must appear), "Any of" (at least one must appear), and "None of" (excluded if any appears). For example, All of "Apple", Any of "MacBook iPhone", None of "ad" matches articles about Apple's MacBook or iPhone that aren't ads.
  • Add a rule straight from the sidebar: right-click a folder or subscription and choose "Add Rule for This Folder…" or "Add Rule for This Subscription…" to start with that scope, or use "Add Rule…" in the right-click menu or the + button.
  • Rules can now be edited. Click the pencil (or double-click a rule) in Settings > Rules, or choose "Edit Rule…" on a collected list in the sidebar.

item.title: Brisk 0.9.0
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Duplicate articles are grouped. When the same article arrives from several subscriptions (the same link, or the same title from another subscription within two days), the list shows it once with "+N more". Reading one marks the copies as read, a copy of an article you've already read arrives as read, and you won't be notified about it again. The article header lists the other subscriptions it came from. You can turn this off in Settings > List.
  • Keyword rules can collect articles into a list. Choose "Collect in List" in Settings > Rules and the list appears under Smart Lists in the sidebar, like Today, with its unread count. It includes existing articles right away. Rules can now also be limited to a single folder.
  • New articles no longer make you lose your place. If new articles arrive above while you're scrolled down, the list stays where you were and a "N New" button appears; click it to jump to the top. Home and End scroll the list to the top or bottom, ⌘↑ and ⌘↓ select the first or last article, and clicking the selected sidebar item again scrolls back to the top.

item.title: Brisk 0.8.1
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Sidebar folders: a single click now shows all articles in the folder without collapsing it. Double-click a folder (or click its disclosure arrow) to collapse or expand it; the article list is not reloaded.
  • Site icons that failed to download because the network was unavailable are retried after an hour, without restarting the app.
  • Fetching the full article now stops right away when you move to another article.

item.title: Brisk 0.8.0
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Keyword rules: in Settings > Rules, set a keyword and choose what happens when a new article's title (or title and content) contains it — mark it as read, star it, or get a notification even if the subscription's notifications are off. Rules can apply to all subscriptions or just one, and can also be applied to articles you already have.
  • Reading settings: in Settings > Reading, choose the font, text size, line spacing, and text width for articles. You can also use View > Bigger Text (⌘+), Smaller Text (⌘−), and Default Text Size (⌘0). Changes apply instantly without losing your place.
  • Export starred articles to a single HTML or Markdown file from the File menu. Useful as a backup, since older articles can disappear from feeds.

item.title: Brisk 0.7.2
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Changing the default refresh interval in Settings > Refresh now takes effect right away. Previously, the new interval only applied after each subscription's next scheduled refresh, so shortening it from 15 to 5 minutes could still wait up to 15 minutes.

item.title: Brisk 0.7.1
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • The article header now shows the site icon next to the feed name.

item.title: Brisk 0.7.0
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • New "Today" smart list in the sidebar shows articles published since midnight. It can also be chosen in widgets.
  • The article list now shows a small picture for each article, taken from the feed or the first image in the article. Only visible rows are loaded. You can turn this off in Settings > List.
  • New option in Settings > List: mark articles as read when you scroll past them.
  • Quiet hours: in Settings > Notifications, choose a time range when Brisk won't send new-article notifications. Articles are still downloaded.
  • The menu bar icon is larger and easier to see.

item.title: Brisk 0.6.4
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Subscriptions now show their site icons in the sidebar and next to the feed name in the article list. Subscriptions with notifications turned on show a small bell next to their name.
  • Search is faster and more accurate. It no longer matches text hidden inside HTML markup, such as link addresses or style names, and it still finds parts of words.
  • After updating, articles you already have are added to the search index in the background. Until that finishes, some older articles may not appear in search results.
